name: Question 9
problem:
Consider the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant $2\times 2$ matrix. Let $Φ(t)$ be a fundamental matrix for this system. A derivation showing that $Φ(t)$ satisfies the matrix differential equation ${Φ}^{′}(t)=A\,Φ(t)$ is given below.

*Hint: $[a,\,b]$ denotes a matrix whose columns are vectors $a$ and $b.$*

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let $Φ(t)=[{x}_{1}(t),\,{x}_{2}(t)]$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{1}^{′}(t)=A{x}_{1}(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ ${x}_{2}^{′}(t)=A{x}_{2}(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}(t)=[{x}_{1}^{′}(t),\,{x}_{2}^{′}(t)]$

$\text{L5}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}(t)=[A{x}_{1}(t),\,A{x}_{2}(t)]$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}(t)=A[{x}_{1}(t),\,{x}_{2}(t)]$

$\text{L7}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}(t)=AΦ(t)$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from the fact that {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from line $\text{L4}$ and substitution from lines {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L5}$ by {{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider line $\text{L2}.$ Since $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ are linearly independent solutions of the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ This means that each column satisfies the differential equation. In particular, 

$$
{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=A{x}_{1}(t).
$$

Therefore, $\text{L2}$ follows from the fact that ${x}_{1}\text{ is a solution of the system}.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L4}$ and $\text{L5}.$ By definition, the derivative of $Φ(t)$ is obtained by differentiating each column,

$$
{Φ}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\,| & | \\ {x}_{1}^{′}(t) & {x}_{2}^{′}(t) \\ \,| & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Using ${x}_{1}^{′}(t)=A{x}_{1}(t)$ from $\text{L2}$ and ${x}_{2}^{′}(t)=A{x}_{2}(t)$ from $\text{L3},$ we substitute each derivative into the matrix to get

$$
{Φ}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\,| & | \\ A{x}_{1}(t) & A{x}_{2}(t) \\ \,| & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L4}$ by substitution from $\text{L2}\text{ and }\text{L3}.$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L5}$ and $\text{L6}.$ We now factor the matrix $A$ on the left:

$$
{Φ}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\,| & | \\ A{x}_{1}(t) & A{x}_{2}(t) \\ \,| & |\end{aligned}]=A[\begin{aligned}\,| & | \\ {x}_{1}(t) & {x}_{2}(t) \\ \,| & |\end{aligned}]=AΦ(t)
$$

Therefore, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L5}$ by $\text{factoring out }A\text{ on the left}.$

choices.value: ${x}_{1}$ is a solution of the system

Question 9
?
Consider the system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant 2×2 matrix. Let Φ(t) be a fundamental matrix for this system. A derivation showing that Φ(t) satisfies the matrix differential equation Φ′(t)=AΦ(t) is given below.

Hint: [a,b] denotes a matrix whose columns are vectors a and b.

L1: Let Φ(t)=[x1(t),x2(t)]

L2: x1′(t)=Ax1(t)

L3: x2′(t)=Ax2(t)

L4: Φ′(t)=[x1′(t),x2′(t)]

L5: Φ′(t)=[Ax1(t),Ax2(t)]

L6: Φ′(t)=A[x1(t),x2(t)]

L7: Φ′(t)=AΦ(t)

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

Line L2 follows from the fact that
x1 is differentiable
x1 is a solution of the system
Φ(t) is invertible for all t
x1 is differentiable
A is diagonalizable
.

Line L5 follows from line L4 and substitution from lines
L2 and L3
L1 and L3
L2 and L3
L3 and L4
L1 and L2
.

Line L6 follows from line L5 by
factoring out A on the left
factoring out A on the left
adding Φ(t) to both sides
transposing the matrix
differentiating again
.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let's justify each of the selected steps.

  • We first consider line L2. Since Φ(t) is a fundamental matrix, its columns x1(t) and x2(t) are linearly independent solutions of the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t). This means that each column satisfies the differential equation. In particular, x1′(t)=Ax1(t). Therefore, L2 follows from the fact that x1 is a solution of the system.

  • Next, we consider lines L4 and L5. By definition, the derivative of Φ(t) is obtained by differentiating each column, Φ′(t)=[||x1′(t)x2′(t)||]. Using x1′(t)=Ax1(t) from L2 and x2′(t)=Ax2(t) from L3, we substitute each derivative into the matrix to get Φ′(t)=[||Ax1(t)Ax2(t)||]. Thus, L5 follows from L4 by substitution from L2 and L3.

  • Finally, we consider lines L5 and L6. We now factor the matrix A on the left: Φ′(t)=[||Ax1(t)Ax2(t)||]=A[||x1(t)x2(t)||]=AΦ(t) Therefore, L6 follows from L5 by factoring out A on the left.
